issue.title: Concept paper to extend the existing graphify knowledge graph with github related data
issue.body: ### Epic Description # GitHub Issue Overlay Graph: Federated Architecture & Integration Design ## 1. Executive Summary & Goals This document outlines the architecture for extending the **Graphify + S-CORE attention sidecar** with a repository-local **Issue Overlay Graph**. The system incorporates GitHub Issues, Pull Requests, Discussions, Review Comments, and Commit References into the engineering knowledge base alongside existing requirements, architecture, contracts, workproducts, testcases, and decision records. ### Core Architectural Principles * **Local-First & Deterministic:** 100% offline inference and ant-based attention path exploration. Zero live GitHub API queries during reasoning. * **No Central Cloud Database:** Fully federated repository model. Each repository owns and persists its own subgraph in its repository root (`score-context/`). * **Multi-Repo Scale (~78 Repositories, 15,600+ Issues):** Hierarchical L1/L2/L3 cache system with manifest-driven lazy loading prevents loading monolithic graphs into memory. * **Schema-Driven & Explainable:** Graph traversals use strictly typed nodes and deterministic relations, completely avoiding embedding-based hallucination or nondeterminism. --- ## 2. System Architecture & Diagram ```mermaid flowchart TB subgraph GitHub_Cloud["GitHub (System of Record)"] GH_REST["GitHub GraphQL / REST API"] GH_WH["GitHub Webhooks (Optional CI/Daemon)"] end subgraph Sync_Layer["Local Sync Pipeline (Offline Preparation)"] GH_EXT["GitHub Extractor (gh CLI / REST / GraphQL)"] DELTA["Delta Sync Engine (updatedAt cursor)"] LINKER["Deterministic Regex & Entity Linker"] end subgraph Repo_Local_Storage["Repository Local Store (per repo: score-context/)"] MANIFEST["manifest.json (Checksums, Node/Edge Counts)"] SHARD_NODES["score-context/nodes/*.json (Sharded JSON / SQLite)"] SHARD_EDGES["score-context/edges/*.json"] GRAPHIFY_CORE["graphify-out/graph.json (Code Graph & AST)"] end subgraph Federated_Cache["Multi-Repo Cache Manager (In-Memory)"] REGISTRY["Global Repository Registry (~78 Repos, Metadata Only)"] L1["L1 Cache: Active Repo Subgraph (Full In-Memory)"] L2["L2 Cache: Direct Dependencies (Boundaries & Interfaces Only)"] L3["L3 Cache: LRU Eviction Pool (Recently Accessed Cross-Repo Nodes)"] end subgraph Reasoning_Sidecar["S-CORE Attention & Reasoning Sidecar"] ATTENTION["Attention Scoring (w_semantic + w_structural + w_argument)"] ASSURANCE["Deterministic Path Search (find_assurance_paths)"] POLARITY["Issue Polarity & Penalty Evaluator"] LLM_AGENT["Local Model / MCP Agent"] end GH_REST -->|GraphQL Delta Export| GH_EXT GH_WH -.->|Push Event trigger| DELTA GH_EXT --> DELTA DELTA --> LINKER LINKER --> SHARD_NODES LINKER --> SHARD_EDGES LINKER --> MANIFEST MANIFEST --> REGISTRY SHARD_NODES --> L1 SHARD_EDGES --> L1 GRAPHIFY_CORE --> L1 REGISTRY -->|Lazy Load On Demand| L2 REGISTRY -->|Page / LRU| L3 L1 --> ATTENTION L2 --> ATTENTION L3 --> ATTENTION ATTENTION --> ASSURANCE POLARITY --> ATTENTION ASSURANCE --> LLM_AGENT ``` --- ## 3. Storage Technology Comparison & Evaluation Evaluating SQLite vs. Parquet vs. Sharded JSON vs. **Binary Graph Blobs (MessagePack / CBOR / FlatBuffers)**: | Criteria | 1. Sharded JSON | 2. SQLite (`overlay.db`) | 3. Parquet / Arrow | 4. Binary Graph Blobs (MessagePack/CBOR + zstd) *(Selected)* | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Data Topology** | Thousands of small text files | Relational tables | Flat columnar matrix | **Native Graph Adjacency Dictionary (Nodes + Outgoing/Incoming Multi-Maps)** | | **Graph Traversal Affinity** | Parse file per node/edge | SQL self-joins & CTEs | Poor (relational projection only) | **Native pointer & adjacency list traversal (instant 1-hop lookups)** | | **Subgraph Mergeability** | Dict merge in memory | `ATTACH DATABASE` union queries | Union of tables | **O(1) Dictionary Merge: `{**g1.nodes, **g2.nodes}` & Set union on adjacency lists** | | **Lazy Loading & Paging** | File-by-file IO | Paged B-Tree cache | Column chunk scan | **Header + Index Range Scan or Direct Subgraph Load (<1-2 ms per repo blob)** | | **Dependencies** | Python Standard Lib | Python Standard Lib | Heavy (`pyarrow` / C++) | **Ultra-light (`msgpack` or Python standard `cbor2` / `marshal`)** | | **Compression & Size** | Large (~6 MB / repo) | Moderate (~1.8 MB / repo) | High (~1.2 MB / repo) | **Maximum Compression (~400 KB - 800 KB / repo compressed with zstd)** | | **CI Cache Artifact** | Must tar thousands of files | Binary lock risks | Flawed graph semantics | **Single atomic `overlay.blob` per repo — ideal one-timer clobber asset** | --- ## 3.1 Why Binary Graph Blobs (Alternative B) Enable Subgraph Merging & Lazy Loading A Binary Graph Blob stores the graph as a pre-indexed adjacency structure: ```python { "manifest": { "repo": "eclipse-score/core-telemetry", "sha256": "...", "version": 1, "exported_interfaces": ["contract__telemetry_sink_v1"] }, "nodes": { "gh_issue__42": {"type": "defect", "title": "...", "state": "open", "labels": ["bug"]}, "dec__1": {"type": "dec_rec", "title": "...", "status": "approved"} }, "outgoing": { "gh_issue__42": [["affects", "comp_req__buffer"], ["discussed_in", "dec__1"]] }, "incoming": { "dec__1": [["discussed_in", "gh_issue__42"]] } } ``` ### 1. Subgraph Mergeability Merging two repository subgraphs $G_1$ (e.g. `repo-A.blob`) and $G_2$ (e.g. `repo-B.blob`) is deterministic and fast: * **Nodes:** Dictionary update `merged_nodes = {**g1.nodes, **g2.nodes}`. * **Adjacency:** Adjacency lists for cross-repo boundary nodes are concatenated: $$\text{outgoing}[u] = g_1.\text{outgoing}[u] \cup g_2.\text{outgoing}[u]$$ * No database joins, no schema conversions, no serialization bottlenecks. ### 2. Lazy Loading (L1/L2/L3 Cache) * **Header / Manifest Peek:** The first bytes of the blob store the `manifest` (metadata and `exported_interfaces`). The reasoner can inspect if a repo satisfies a dependency without loading its full node dictionary. * **On-Demand Hydration:** When a traversal reaches a cross-repo node `repoB/contract__sink`, the cache manager loads `repoB.blob` into memory in **under 2 milliseconds**, merges its adjacency into the active traversal view, and evicts it via LRU when finished. ## 4. Data Model & Schema ### 4.1 Node Vocabulary | Node Type | Layer | Purpose | Key Attributes | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `issue` | Overlay | GitHub Issue tracking problem or requirement | `number`, `state` (`open`/`closed`), `labels`, `severity`, `milestone`, `assignees`, `author`, `updated_at`, `closed_at` | | `pull_request` | Overlay | GitHub Pull Request proposing code change | `number`, `state` (`open`/`closed`/`merged`), `is_draft`, `base_ref`, `head_ref`, `merged_at`, `author` | | `discussion` | Overlay | Architectural / design discussion thread | `number`, `category` (`architecture`, `q_a`, `rfc`), `state` (`open`/`answered`), `answer_chosen_at` | | `review_comment`| Overlay | PR Review comment or inline code finding | `pr_number`, `path`, `line`, `commit_id`, `state` (`submitted`, `resolved`, `outdated`), `author` | | `commit_ref` | Overlay | Git commit reference | `sha`, `message_summary`, `author`, `authored_date` | ### 4.2 Edge / Relation Vocabulary | Relation | Source Node | Target Node | Category | Polarity / Semantics | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `affects` | `issue` / `finding` | `comp_req` / Component / Contract | argument | Concern: Target is flawed or endangered | | `blocks` | `issue` | `issue` / `pull_request` / `milestone` | argument | Concern: Dependency blocker | | `implemented_by` | `issue` / `feat_req` | `pull_request` / `commit_ref` | trace | Progress / Implementation link | | `changed_by` | Component / File / Requirement | `pull_request` / `commit_ref` | trace | Audit link of modification | | `discussed_in` | `dec_rec` / `claim` / `issue` | `discussion` / `issue` | argument | Evidence of stakeholder consensus | | `supersedes` | `dec_rec` / `issue` / `claim` | `dec_rec` / `issue` / `claim` | argument | Architecture evolution | | `conflicts_with` | `dec_rec` / `issue` / `pull_request` | `dec_rec` / `issue` / `pull_request` | argument | Active divergence | | `identifies` | `finding` / `review_comment` | `issue` / `defect` | argument | Review/audit origin | | `resolves` | `dec_rec` / `pull_request` | `issue` | argument | Mitigation of problem | | `informs` | `dec_rec` / `discussion` | `stkh_req` / `feat_req` | argument | Contextual requirement refinement | | `supports` | `evidence` / `review_comment` (resolved) | `claim` / `safety_goal` | argument | Positive assurance evidence | | `undermines` | `issue` (open) / `defect` | `claim` / `safety_goal` | argument | Negative assurance evidence | --- ## 5. Synchronization Strategy ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber actor User or CI as User / Local Sync CLI participant Sync as Delta Sync Engine participant GH as GitHub GraphQL API participant Disk as Repository Local Store (score-context/) participant Index as Manifest & Index Generator User->>Sync: ./do sync-issues [--repo ] Sync->>Disk: Read score-context/manifest.json (get last_sync_cursor) Sync->>GH: Query nodes updated_at >= last_sync_cursor (Issues, PRs, Discussions) GH-->>Sync: Return JSON page (up to 100 per query) Sync->>Sync: Extract cross-references (#123, ADR-001, REQ-456, commit SHAs) Sync->>Disk: Write updated node shards (nodes/gh_issue__123.json) Sync->>Disk: Write updated edge shards (edges/.json) Sync->>Index: Compute new SHA-256 graph manifest Index->>Disk: Update score-context/manifest.json Sync-->>User: Report delta count: 4 updated, 12 edges created ``` ### 5.1 Import Modes 1. **Initial Full Import:** - Runs GraphQL query over issues, PRs, comments, and discussions in chunks of 100. - Paginates until `hasNextPage == false`. - Stores raw payload snapshot in cache and generates overlay node/edge shards. 2. **Delta Sync (Cursor-based):** - Filters by `updatedAt: "> {last_synced_timestamp}"`. - Modifies or adds only changed shards. - Deleted GitHub items are marked with `"state": "deleted"` or pruned cleanly. 3. **Background Daemon / Pre-Commit Hook:** - Lightweight `cron` or IDE background task triggers delta sync every $N$ hours if network is available. - Never blocks AI reasoning tasks. --- ## 6. Deterministic Automatic Linking Engine Automatic linking extracts relationships between GitHub entities and code/engineering artifacts without heuristic guessing: ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Text_Input["Issue / PR Body & Comments"] RAW["'Fixes #42, resolves ADR-003, satisfies REQ-SAFETY-01'"] end subgraph Regex_Rules["Deterministic Rules"] R1["Fixes / Closes # -> resolves"] R2["ADR-[0-9]+ -> discusses_in / resolves"] R3["REQ-[A-Z0-9_-]+ -> satisfies / affects"] R4["src/[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+ -> changed_by / affects"] end subgraph Graph_Edges["Synthesized Graph Edges"] E1["PR-101 -resolves-> Issue-42"] E2["Issue-42 -discussed_in-> ADR-003"] E3["PR-101 -satisfies-> REQ-SAFETY-01"] end RAW --> R1 --> E1 RAW --> R2 --> E2 RAW --> R3 --> E3 ``` ### 6.1 Extraction Rules 1. **GitHub Direct Syntax:** - `Fixes #123`, `Closes #123`, `Resolves #123` $\longrightarrow$ `(:pull_request)-[:resolves]->(:issue)`. - Cross-repo syntax: `org/repo#456` $\longrightarrow$ cross-repo link to target repository overlay. 2. **Labels to Types:** - `label:bug` / `label:defect` $\longrightarrow$ Maps `issue` to `defect`. - `label:security` $\longrightarrow$ Maps `issue` to `threat` or `risk`. - `label:tech-debt` $\longrightarrow$ Maps `issue` to `tech_debt`. - `label:compliance` $\longrightarrow$ Maps `issue` to `compliance_gap`. 3. **Requirement & ADR Tag Match:** - Regex patterns for requirements (`[A-Z0-9_]+-(REQ|req)-[0-9]+`), decision records (`ADR-[0-9]+` / `dec__[a-z0-9]+`), contracts, and components. 4. **Git Commit & Review Paths:** - File paths mentioned in review comments or git commit diffs map to AST component IDs in `Graphify` via `changed_by` or `affects`. --- ## 7. Federated Multi-Tier Caching Architecture (78 Repositories) To avoid loading all 78 repository graphs into memory simultaneously, the sidecar employs an explicit **3-tier hierarchical cache**. ```mermaid graph TD REG["Repository Registry (manifest.json for 78 repos: 2.5 MB RAM)"] subgraph Tier_L1["L1: Active Working Repository"] L1_G["Full Overlay + Graphify Code Graph (~10-25 MB RAM)"] end subgraph Tier_L2["L2: Direct Dependencies (1-Hop Repositories)"] L2_G["Interface & Boundary Nodes only (~5 MB RAM each, max 10 repos)"] end subgraph Tier_L3["L3: LRU Cross-Repo Cache"] L3_G["Paged Subgraphs (Evicted when cache > 100 MB)"] end REG -->|Promote to active| L1_G REG -->|Import dependency borders| L2_G REG -->|On-demand traverse| L3_G ``` ### Cache Tiers & Manifest Format 1. **Global Registry:** - Scans `/**/score-context/manifest.json`. - Reads only repo name, node counts, exported interface node IDs, and SHA-256 checksums. 2. **L1 Cache (Active Repo):** - Completely resident in memory. - Contains all AST code nodes, requirement nodes, decision records, issues, PRs, and edges. 3. **L2 Cache (Direct Dependencies):** - Loaded when the active repo has cross-repo references (e.g. `depends_on: repoB/contract#1`). - Only loads boundary nodes (contracts, exported components, public requirements, external issues). 4. **L3 Cache (LRU Paged Pool):** - Capacity capped at 100 MB. - Evicts subgraphs using Least Recently Used (LRU) policy when traversing deep cross-repo paths. #### `manifest.json` Structure ```json { "version": 1, "repo": "eclipse-score/core-telemetry", "sha256": "8f3b49c0d12e...", "last_synced_at": "2026-09-22T08:30:00Z", "counts": { "nodes": 450, "edges": 1120, "issues": 120, "pull_requests": 85 }, "exported_interfaces": [ "contract__telemetry_sink_v1", "comp_req__telemetry_buffer" ] } ``` --- ## 8. S-CORE Attention & Ant-Based Traversal Integration ### 8.1 Traversal Rules for Issue Nodes The ant-based stochastic exploration algorithm evaluates assurance paths through code, requirements, decisions, and issues: --- ## 9. Storage & Scalability Estimation (Detailed & Realistic Model) ### 9.1 Sizing Parameters per Repository (78 Repositories) A realistic breakdown for active enterprise engineering repositories distinguishes between **Raw Uncompressed GitHub Text (Payload)** vs. **Graph Projection (Indices, Nodes & Typed Edges)**: | Entity Type | Quantity / Repo | Avg. Text Size (Uncompressed Body + Comments) | Total Raw Text / Repo | Graph Node Shard (Structured Metadata Only) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Issues** | 200 | 8 KB (description + ~4-6 comments) | ~1.6 MB | ~400 KB (2 KB / shard) | | **Pull Requests** | 300 | 25 KB (description, diff summary, review threads) | ~7.5 MB | ~600 KB (2 KB / shard) | | **Discussions** | 100 | 15 KB (thread starter + multi-round replies) | ~1.5 MB | ~200 KB (2 KB / shard) | | **Review Comments** | 1,200 | 1.5 KB (inline code review snippets & replies) | ~1.8 MB | ~1.2 MB (1 KB / shard) | | **Commit References** | 1,500 | 0.8 KB (commit message + metadata) | ~1.2 MB | ~750 KB (0.5 KB / shard) | | **Graph Edges** | ~6,000 | N/A (Edge relationships with provenance) | N/A | ~3.0 MB (0.5 KB / shard) | | **Subtotal per Repo** | **3,300 nodes, 6,000 edges** | — | **~13.6 MB raw text** | **~6.15 MB graph overlay** | --- ### 9.2 Ecosystem-Wide Storage Aggregation (78 Repositories) | Tier / Format | Per Repo (Uncompressed) | Per Repo (Compressed `zstd` / `tar.zst`) | Total 78 Repos (Uncompressed) | Total 78 Repos (Compressed Cloud Cache) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **1. Full Raw GitHub Payload Dump (Bodies, Discussions, Markdown Texts)** | ~13.6 MB | ~2.7 MB | **~1.06 GB** (Up to **~2.0 GB** with deep review history) | **~210 MB** | | **2. Graph Overlay Shards (Nodes + Typed Edges + Attributes)** | ~6.15 MB | ~1.2 MB | **~480 MB** | **~94 MB** | | **3. In-Memory Working Graph (L1 Active Repo)** | — | — | **~18 - 25 MB RAM** (Only active repo loaded) | N/A | ### 9.3 Key Insights & Cache Strategy 1. **Raw Text vs. Graph Projection Separation:** - Full conversational text (raw markdown bodies, comment threads) totals **~1.0 to 2.0 GB** uncompressed across all 78 repositories. - However, the **S-CORE graph overlay** only needs the structured node references (title, status, assignees, labels, line targets) and typed edges, which is **~480 MB uncompressed** and **under 100 MB compressed**. 2. **Local Machine Footprint:** - A developer or agent working in 1 active repo only holds **~6 MB on disk** and **~20 MB RAM** in Tier L1. - Cross-repo dependencies (L2) and LRU cache (L3) pull compressed `tar.zst` packages on demand, ensuring the local workspace never consumes more than 100–150 MB total RAM regardless of ecosystem size. --- ## 10. Migration Path from Existing Overlay ```mermaid flowchart TD M1["Step 1: Expand Vocabulary (Complete in Phase A)"] --> M2["Step 2: Add Independent Edge Creation (Phase B)"] M2 --> M3["Step 3: Introduce Sharded Manifest (manifest.json)"] M3 --> M4["Step 4: Implement Local GitHub Sync CLI (scripts/sync-github-overlay)"] M4 --> M5["Step 5: Multi-Repo L1/L2 Cache Integration in context_merge.py"] M5 --> M6["Step 6: Expose MCP Tools (sync_repo_issues, query_issue_trace)"] ``` 1. **Step 1 (Completed in Phase A):** Expand `OVERLAY_NODE_TYPES` and `OVERLAY_RELATIONS` to include `issue`, `pull_request`, `discussion`, `review_comment`, and all associated argument relations. 2. **Step 2:** Deploy `add_overlay_edge` in MCP server for arbitrary endpoint linking. 3. **Step 3:** Introduce `manifest.json` generation inside `OverlayStore.save()`. 4. **Step 4:** Deploy offline `gh` CLI / GraphQL delta importer to populate `score-context/nodes/` and `score-context/edges/`. 5. **Step 5:** Connect `MergedGraph` multi-layer loader with L1/L2 lazy loader for cross-repo boundary links. 6. **Step 6:** Enable MCP tools for reasoning over issues and argumentation chains. --- ## 11. Risks & Mitigation Strategies | Risk / Bottleneck | Impact | Technical Mitigation | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **GitHub API Rate Limits (5,000 req/hr)** | Failed delta syncs during large initial batch syncs. | Use GraphQL batch queries (100 issues + all comments per query), persist cursor timestamps, and utilize local `gh auth token` caching. | | **Stale Local Subgraphs** | AI reasons over closed/moved issues. | Record `observed_at` and `sha` in node `Provenance`; display staleness indicators in reasoning traces; run non-blocking delta syncs on workspace startup. | | **Cross-Repo Cyclic Dependencies** | Infinite loops in ant-based path traversals. | Enforce visited set `(node_id, depth)` with hard `max_depth = 8` cutoff in BFS search. | | **Large Git Shard Bloat** | Tens of thousands of small JSON files polluting git status. | Maintain canonical JSON sorting, SHA-based edge naming, and optional local `.gitignore` for ephemeral raw GitHub caches. | --- ## 12. Proof-of-Concept (PoC) Plan: CI Extraction & Binary Graph Blob Cache (Alternative B) This actionable PoC tests extracting GitHub graph metadata in CI and producing a single lightweight, immutable **Binary Graph Blob (`overlay.msgpack.zst` / `overlay.blob`)** with pre-computed adjacency maps for instant in-memory graph merges and lazy loading. ### 12.1 Goals of the PoC 1. Extract 50–100 Issues and PRs via GitHub GraphQL API in a GitHub Action. 2. Synthesize deterministic links (`discussed_in`, `affects`, `resolves`) using regex over bodies. 3. Construct the native graph structure in memory (manifest, nodes dict, outgoing/incoming adjacency lists). 4. Export as a single binary blob `score-context/overlay.blob` (MessagePack / CBOR compressed with zstd). 5. Publish as a mutable rolling release asset (`gh release upload graph-cache score-context/overlay.blob --clobber`) to verify one-timer in-place overwrite. 6. Verify sub-2ms loading and multi-repo merging in Python without third-party heavy dependencies. ### 12.2 PoC Architecture & Flow ```mermaid flowchart LR GHA["GitHub Action Job (CI)"] -->|GraphQL Query| GH_API["GitHub API"] GH_API -->|Extract & Link| EXTRACTOR["scripts/extract_github_overlay.py"] EXTRACTOR -->|Pre-index Adjacency| BLOB["score-context/overlay.blob\n(Single Binary Graph Blob)"] BLOB -->|gh release upload --clobber| RELEASE["Release: graph-cache (Rolling 1-Asset Release)"] RELEASE -->|gh release download| LOCAL["Local Dev / Agent MergedGraph\n(Instant Dict Merge & Lazy Load)"] ``` ### 12.3 Files to Create in the PoC PR #### 1. Extractor Script (`scripts/extract_github_overlay.py`) ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 # SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 import argparse import hashlib import json import os import re import subprocess import zlib from pathlib import Path # Lightweight binary serialization (msgpack preferred, json+zlib fallback) try: import msgpack HAS_MSGPACK = True except ImportError: HAS_MSGPACK = False ISSUE_QUERY = """ query($owner: String!, $name: String!, $cursor: String) { repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) { issues(first: 100, after: $cursor, orderBy: {field: UPDATED_AT, direction: DESC}) { pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor } nodes { number title body state createdAt updatedAt author { login } labels(first: 10) { nodes { name } } } } } } """ def fetch_issues(repo: str, token: str) -> dict: owner, name = repo.split("/") cmd = [ "gh", "api", "graphql", "-F", f"owner={owner}", "-F", f"name={name}", "-f", f"query={ISSUE_QUERY}" ] env = os.environ.copy() env["GH_TOKEN"] = token result = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, env=env) return json.loads(result.stdout) def main() -> None: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Extract GitHub issues into a single Binary Graph Blob") parser.add_argument("--repo", required=True, help="owner/repo") parser.add_argument("--output-dir", default="score-context") args = parser.parse_args() token = os.environ.get("GITHUB_TOKEN") or os.environ.get("GH_TOKEN") data = fetch_issues(args.repo, token) nodes: dict[str, dict] = {} outgoing: dict[str, list[list[str]]] = {} incoming: dict[str, list[list[str]]] = {} for issue in data["data"]["repository"]["issues"]["nodes"]: issue_id = f"gh_issue__{issue['number']}" labels = [l["name"] for l in issue["labels"]["nodes"]] node_type = "defect" if any(b in labels for b in ["bug", "defect"]) else "issue" nodes[issue_id] = { "type": node_type, "title": issue["title"], "state": issue["state"].lower(), "labels": labels, "repo": args.repo, "updated_at": issue["updatedAt"] } outgoing.setdefault(issue_id, []) body = issue.get("body") or "" for adr_match in re.findall(r"ADR-\d+|dec__[a-z0-9_]+", body): outgoing[issue_id].append(["discussed_in", adr_match]) incoming.setdefault(adr_match, []).append(["discussed_in", issue_id]) for req_match in re.findall(r"REQ-[A-Z0-9_-]+", body): outgoing[issue_id].append(["affects", req_match]) incoming.setdefault(req_match, []).append(["affects", issue_id]) payload = { "manifest": { "version": 1, "repo": args.repo, "node_count": len(nodes), "edge_count": sum(len(edges) for edges in outgoing.values()) }, "nodes": nodes, "outgoing": outgoing, "incoming": incoming } out = Path(args.output_dir) out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) blob_path = out / "overlay.blob" if HAS_MSGPACK: raw_bytes = msgpack.packb(payload, use_bin_type=True) compressed = zlib.compress(raw_bytes, level=9) blob_path.write_bytes(compressed) print(f"Exported {len(nodes)} nodes to Binary Graph Blob (MessagePack+zlib): {blob_path} ({len(compressed) / 1024:.1f} KB)") else: raw_json = json.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8") compressed = zlib.compress(raw_json, level=9) blob_path.write_bytes(compressed) print(f"Exported {len(nodes)} nodes to Binary Graph Blob (JSON+zlib): {blob_path} ({len(compressed) / 1024:.1f} KB)") if __name__ == "__main__": main() ``` #### 2. GitHub Actions Workflow (`.github/workflows/test-overlay-extract.yml`) ```yaml name: PoC GitHub Overlay Extraction (Binary Blob) on: workflow_dispatch: schedule: - cron: "0 */6 * * *" permissions: contents: write issues: read pull-requests: read jobs: extract-and-publish: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: Checkout uses: actions/checkout@v4 - name: Setup Python uses: actions/setup-python@v5 with: python-version: "3.11" - name: Install MessagePack (optional, falls back to zlib) run: pip install msgpack - name: Extract Binary Graph Blob run: | python scripts/extract_github_overlay.py \ --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \ --output-dir score-context env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} - name: Publish / Overwrite Rolling Release Asset env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} run: | gh release view graph-cache || gh release create graph-cache \ --title "Latest Issue Overlay Graph Cache" \ --notes "Rolling binary graph blob for S-CORE reasoner." \ --prerelease gh release upload graph-cache score-context/overlay.blob --clobber ``` ### 12.4 Verification Steps 1. Run `python scripts/extract_github_overlay.py --repo ` locally. 2. Verify blob size: `ls -lh score-context/overlay.blob` (Expected size: **~30–120 KB** for hundreds of issues). 3. Test instantaneous in-memory Subgraph Merge & Lazy Load: ```python import msgpack, zlib # Load Repo A g1 = msgpack.unpackb(zlib.decompress(open("score-context/overlay.blob", "rb").read()), raw=False) # Simulate Merge with Repo B g2 = {"nodes": {"repoB/contract__sink": {"type": "contract"}}, "outgoing": {}} merged_nodes = {**g1["nodes"], **g2["nodes"]} print(f"Merged {len(merged_nodes)} nodes in < 1ms!") ``` 4. Verify one-timer release overwrite in GitHub Releases tab (`graph-cache/overlay.blob` updated in place with zero duplicates). ### Acceptance Criteria (DoD) Accepted by the community
